correctness.rationale: Substitution in either implicit stage equation yields R=1−r/(1+ru). The inverse map u=(1−R)^{-1}−1/r gives multiplier density (1−R)^{-2} on [1−r,1/(1+r)]. Integrating over [−t,t] and clipping at the two endpoints verifies each quantile branch: before clipping the CDF is 2t/(1−t²); afterward it is 1/(1−t)−1/r or 1+1/r−1/(1+t). The endpoint magnitudes tie exactly at r=√2. As stated by continuity, the quantile at p=0 is its support endpoint (the literal infimum over all real x at p=0 would instead be −∞; the continuous convention affects no integrals or couplings). The layer-cake Fréchet lower bound is attained by opposite response ranks. The joint survival probabilities are continuous because the response marginals have no atoms, so equality of integrals forces equality in the bound everywhere; disintegration over g=R² gives uniform-stage lifts. For r≤1 strict monotonicity forces ordinary antithetic stages. For each r>1 both g(u) and g(1−u) strictly decrease on a nontrivial initial interval, which rules out opposite response ranks and permits a strictly improving equal-length partner exchange.
